title: Introduction
author: 3iGR44tcGMnRnhEYm
chapter_outcomes: Recall the reactions by which carboxylic acids can be produced: (a) oxidation of primary alcohols and aldehydes with acidified $\mathrm{K_2 Cr_2 O_7}$ or acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and refluxing (b) hydrolysis of nitriles with dilute acid or dilute alkali followed by acidification (c) hydrolysis of esters with dilute acid or dilute alkali  and heat followed by acidification

Describe the redox reaction with reactive metals to produce a salt and $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$, the neutralisation reaction with alkalis to produce a salt and $\mathrm{H_2 O(l)}$, the acid–base reaction with carbonates to produce a salt and $\mathrm{H_2 O(l)}$ and $\mathrm{CO_2 (g)}$, esterification with alcohols with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2 SO_4}$ as catalyst, and reduction by $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ to form a primary alcohol
